headline: A 2019 law extends several expiring Department of Veterans Affairs programs, including housing support for very low-income veteran families, for one or two more fiscal years.
what_it_does: This law keeps several Department of Veterans Affairs programs from ending on their scheduled dates. It extends a set of VA authorities through fiscal year 2020, including vendee loans, beneficiary travel, and a regional office in the Philippines. It also extends through fiscal year 2021 the authority to fund supportive services for very low-income veteran families living in permanent housing.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who use VA beneficiary travel benefits
who_it_affects.how: The law keeps the VA's authority to pay travel costs for eligible veterans going to VA medical appointments and related care through the extended period.

who_it_affects.group: Very low-income veteran families in permanent housing
who_it_affects.how: The law keeps federal funding available for supportive services, such as help that keeps them stably housed, through fiscal year 2021.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who use VA vendee loans
who_it_affects.how: The law keeps the VA's authority for vendee loans, which help buyers of VA-acquired property, in place through fiscal year 2020.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans and families served by the VA regional office in the Philippines
who_it_affects.how: The law keeps this regional office authorized to operate through fiscal year 2020.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 30, 2019; the extended authorities run through fiscal year 2020 for most programs and fiscal year 2021 for the supportive housing services authority.
